issue.title: Review the lemma 6a and 6b1 disc certificate code independently

milestone.title: G2 · Theorem A(M = 5)
milestone.description: Wire the review's control fixes into the M = 5 certificate, certify lemmas 6a(5) and 6b1, review them independently, and write up Theorem A(M = 5).

issue.body:
**What.** A fresh agent, given the code and the statements but not the notes' reasoning, re-implements the disc covering check in other arithmetic.

**Why.** AGENTS.md: new certificate code gets an independent review before its claim is relied on.

**Found in sweep:** notes/PROOF_QUEUE.md P2: lemma 6b1's discs are still not checked; proof/A_lemmas_M.md: the disc certificates are not yet reviewed.

**Acceptance (each can fail).**
- The second implementation agrees on every disc, and the shared machinery is recorded.
- Mutations (a dropped disc, a scaled radius) fail in both.
- Needs Nathan's approval of the subagent and its number.

**Files.** [solver/proof/lemma6b1_disc.py](https://github.com/nmoinvaz/choptuik-large-d/blob/main/solver/proof/lemma6b1_disc.py), [proof/A_lemmas_M.md](https://github.com/nmoinvaz/choptuik-large-d/blob/main/proof/A_lemmas_M.md), [notes/PROOF_QUEUE.md](https://github.com/nmoinvaz/choptuik-large-d/blob/main/notes/PROOF_QUEUE.md)

comments.body: started: independent reviewer subagent of the coordinator, on the Apple M5 Mac (`mac`). Checkout: worktree `.claude/worktrees/agent-ab6ec531e45efaac2` at `ac2c2fc`, backup branch `wip/i39`. Threads: at most 2 processes under `nice -n 10` (another agent, #106, shares the machine). Raw output to `I39-mac/` in choptuik-large-d-raw.

Progress (mac, 16:33 UTC). Two processes at nice 10: the input regeneration at 99% cpu and 61 MB, the review's disc check at 100% cpu and 49 MB. Machine load 3.4, 56% idle.

The stored rows keep only each disc's verdict and Λ, not the Lohner box the disc lemma was given. So `review_39/dump_inputs.py` reruns the original `row_run` unchanged on the stored C¹ ray and records each disc's exact arguments. On rows 17 and 16 the regenerated boxes have the stored box radii bit for bit, and the original certify gives the stored Λ to 1e-13.

The review's disc lemma (`check_6b1.py`, mpmath intervals, no python-flint) has certified all 10 discs of row 17 and 5 of row 16 so far. Its Λ is 0.5–5% below the original's, because its Jacobian enclosure wraps less. The transcription of the system matches `SysUM.rhs` and `.lin` to 2e-16, and the sign mutation of that comparison fires. The covering geometry gives the original's counts exactly (366 tiles, 1188 pieces, 957 links). Its C1 waits for the remaining rows.

The 6a final step re-evaluated from the stored B gives ρ₆ₐ ≤ 0.0790, against the original's 0.231. Both are valid bounds. The gap comes from the original's `acb_mat.inv`, whose enclosure of G_slow⁻¹ has radius 4.1 on entries of size at most 1.54. A preconditioned inverse is tight (‖I − R G_slow‖ ≤ 5e-4), and a float evaluation gives 0.0789. The mutations coords, partial and Bscale fail in both codes. One finding is under investigation, and I will report it in the summary. Projected end of the disc work is about 18:30 UTC.

Progress (mac, 17:31 UTC). Two workers at nice 10, each at about 100% cpu, using 43 MB and 76 MB. The machine is shared with #106, load 6–13, so input regeneration ran at about a third of macm3's speed: row 15 took 36 min. Each worker now regenerates one row's inputs and checks them, the two working from opposite ends.

- **6b₁ discs.** The review's disc lemma has certified all 23 discs of rows 17 and 16. Rows 15–0 are in progress.
- **6b₁ mutations so far:**
  - The sign mutation (V_u = +V/2 in the defect) certifies 0 of 10 discs of row 17 in both codes.
  - A disc radius ×1.01 still certifies all 10 discs of row 17 in both codes (Λ +2%). The claim stays true, so this is not a falsifying mutation.
  - The original covering check fails, as it must, with tile (9, 5) dropped, with row 9's stored r ×1.01 (design mismatch), and with G₀'s radius ×1.01 (402 → 406.02, so s₀ = 405 e^{−3iπ/4} is not in G₀).
- **6a, a discrepancy in the run's inputs.** `lemma6_jump_M.py` reads the box centre from the box file's key `x`, falling back to `FPM.ZEROS[5]`. `certify_M2.py export6a` writes the centre under `p` and has no `x`. So the backward flow and the coordinate change at ξ_a used w = W0·(x̂₁ ± 1e-18), with x̂₁ = 0.999228404 (the stored double-precision zero). The certificate's centre is p̂₁ = 0.9992284032065677…, 7.9e-10 away. The stored B is therefore not proven to enclose DΦ at the certificate's parameters.
  - A double-precision integration by a second route (`b_float.py`, the (P, V, C) u-form with DOP853) reproduces mid(B) to 9.6e-13 at w(x̂). At w(p̂) the result moves by up to 2.8e-6, which is 0.18 of the entry's radius, so it is still inside B.
  - Its control (wf + 1e-6) puts B_float 225 radii outside.
  - A rerun of the backward flow with the right centre is expected to pass. Same code and file format on win2 (#104). This is reported, not fixed.

Progress (mac, 17:54 UTC). Two workers at nice 10, each at 100% cpu, using 76 MB and 46 MB. Machine load 4.1, 56% idle.

- **6b₁ discs.** Rows 0 and 14–17 (93 discs) are all certified by the review's disc lemma. On row 0 its Λ is within 7e-5 of the original's, because the boxes are narrow there. On the inner rows it is 0.5–5% lower. Rows 1–13 are in progress.
- **The ray boxes.** A 192-bit Taylor-series control (`ray_hp.py`, non-rigorous truncation) steps y⁺ at p̂ along the start ray. It lies inside every stored ray box, rows 1–17, at 1e-8 to 1e-11 of the box radius. Its mutation (w × (1 + 1e-12)) puts rows 1–3 outside by 4e4 to 1e5 radii.
- **The arc boxes.** A double-precision control (`lohner_float.py`) integrates each arc from its stored start state. On rows 15–17 it lies inside every regenerated box, at at most 0.0055 of the radius. Its mutation (w × (1 + 1e-6)) puts 30 of 33 outside.
- **Two controls fired on real data in their first versions.** In each case I found the cause in the control itself, not in the certificate, before going on.
  - lohner_float v1 also integrated the ray. Its own double-precision error at |u| = 23.46 (1.8e-12) exceeded the ray box (1.2e-12), and the arc amplified both alike.
  - ray_hp v1 carried interval widths, grown by wrapping, and read them as deviations.
  - Both first-version logs are kept in `I39-mac/`.

Progress (mac, 18:24 UTC). Two workers at nice 10, each at 99% cpu, using 39 MB and 43 MB. Machine load 4.9.

Lemma 6b₁(5): rows 0, 1 and 11–17 are certified by the review's disc lemma, 9 of 18 rows (174 of 366 discs), with no disc failing in either code. Row 2's inputs are regenerated, and rows 2–10 remain, about 75 min at this rate. Raw progress is pushed to `I39-mac/`.

Progress (mac, 18:59 UTC). Two workers at nice 10, each at 95% cpu, using 34 MB and 49 MB. Machine load 6.8.

Lemma 6b₁(5): rows 0–2 and 9–17 are certified by the review, 12 of 18 rows, with no disc failing. The inputs of rows 3 and 8 are regenerated and their checks are running. Rows 4–7 remain, about 45 min.

Progress (mac, 19:43 UTC). Two workers at nice 10, each at 97–98% cpu, using 32 MB and 44 MB. The machine's load average is now 64 from other jobs, so rows 4 and 7 took 24 and 34 min to regenerate.

Lemma 6b₁(5): rows 0–3 and 8–17 are certified by the review, 14 of 18 rows, with no disc failing. The checks of rows 4 and 7 are running, then rows 5 and 6. At this load, the end is about 20:40 UTC.

Progress (mac, 20:12 UTC). Two workers at nice 10. Lemma 6b₁(5): 16 of 18 rows are certified by the review (all but 5 and 6), with no disc failing. The inputs of rows 5 and 6 are regenerated and their checks are running, about 15 min. Then come the covering check, its mutations, the row 0 disc mutations and the closing summary.

## Closing summary: independent review of the 6b₁(5) and 6a(5) certificates Reviewer: an independent subagent of the coordinator, on the Apple M5 Mac. Code: `solver/proof/review_39/` on branch `wip/i39` (head `5151919`). Raw output: `I39-mac/` of the raw-data repository (commit `7bcfbc6`). Versions: python-flint 0.9.0, FLINT 3.6.0, mpmath 1.3.0 (pure-Python backend), numpy 2.5.4, scipy 1.18.1, Python 3.13.15. The tooling did not allow a REPORT.md, so this comment is the report. ### Verdicts **6b₁(5): agrees.** The review's disc lemma, in mpmath interval arithmetic, certifies all 366 discs of rows 0–17 on the original's inputs. No disc disagrees. The review's covering check C1–C8 passes with the original's counts (366 tiles glued, 1188 meeting-set pieces, 957 links). **6a(5): the final step agrees, but the run behind B has a gap.** - From the stored B, the review gets ρ₆ₐ ≤ 0.0790076 < 1. The original gets 0.2310. Both are valid upper bounds; the original's is loose. - The backward flow and the coordinate change were computed with w centred at the stored double-precision zero x̂, not at the certificate's p̂. The two differ by 7.9e-10 in ω/ω∞, against a half-width of 1e-18. So B is not proven to enclose DΦ at the certificate's parameters. - Double-precision evidence says a rerun at p̂ would pass. - The backward flow itself was not re-implemented. ### Lemma 6b₁(5): what was and was not re-checked The stored rows keep each disc's verdict and Λ, not the arguments the disc lemma was given. `dump_inputs.py` reran the original `lemma6b1_cover_M.row_run` unchanged on the stored C¹ ray (`I38-macm3/.../ray.json`). It recorded every disc's exact arguments (centre, Lohner box, w ball, r, n) as mantissa and exponent pairs, in `I39-mac/disc_inputs/`. The regenerated boxes have the stored box radii bit for bit on 274 of 366 discs, including every disc of rows 3–17. On rows 0–2 the step counts are the same, but from disc 3–4 on the radii differ by up to 6% (ratios 0.937–1.052). This is the floating-point QR of another machine, as with win2's ratios of 0.93–1.10, so those discs were checked on equally valid boxes that are not identical to the stored ones. The original certify gives the stored Λ to at most 8.7e-13. `check_6b1.py` is a second implementation of lemma D in mpmath intervals (`civ.py`: rectangular complex intervals on `mpmath.libmp.libmpi` with directed rounding, 128 bits). It imports no python-flint and no code under review, and it uses a different method at each step: | step | original (`lemma6b1_disc_M.certify`) | review (`check_6b1.certify_disc`) | |---|---|---| | Taylor polynomial | Picard iteration on `acb_series` | coefficient recursion on lazy series | | defect Δ | exact high coefficients of F(p) − p′, z a polynomial plus a ζ ball | Taylor model of order n, tail by the triangle inequality, low coefficients checked to contain 0 | | Jacobian L | hand-written `SysUM.lin` | forward-mode derivatives of one transcription of F | | weights | `numpy.linalg.eig` | power iteration | | centre | `leg.xi(t)` | recomputed from ρ_j and t_k, and checked to overlap the stored centre ball on every disc | Per row (`check_6b1.py summary`, `I39-mac/summary_6b1.md`): | row (row 17), because its Jacobian enclosure over the wide box B wraps less. On rows 0–10 the two agree to 5e-4 relative, and there the review's is sometimes the larger, by at most 1.7e-5. The covering check (`check_6b1.py cover`) re-implements C1–C8 on the exact numbers of the design, gluing row by row and checking the connectivity of every meeting set. Its C1 also checks that `ray.json`'s centre is the certificate's p̂, which the original's C1 does not. Controls that share no Lohner code (non-rigorous): - `ray_hp.py` steps y⁺ at p̂ along the start ray by Taylor series at 192 bits. The value lies inside all 17 stored ray boxes, at 1e-8 to 1e-11 of their radius. - `lohner_float.py` integrates rows 15–17's arcs in double precision from their stored start states. The values lie inside all 33 regenerated boxes, at at most 0.0055 of the radius. The other rows' boxes are narrower than double precision. **Not re-checked:** - The Lohner flow itself (`validated_int.Lohner` C¹ mode with `lemma6_common`'s a-priori enclosure), except through the two controls above. - The C¹ start data at s₀ (the old sector lemma of `fixed_point_M`). - G₀ (lemma S and lemma 6b₀ at M = 5). - (H2). ### Lemma 6a(5): what was and was not re-checked `check_6a.py` re-evaluates the final step in mpmath intervals at 256 bits: 1. Λ = max_i Σ_j w_i L_ij / w_j from the exported L and weights. The export is `export_6a_flat.py`, which runs the original lemma S and flat estimate. The result is 0.423326706793, equal to the original's. 2. T at ξ_a, derived from §1 (p = D/ξ, v = S/ξ² − (1 + iμw)D/ξ, c = C), and G = T B on the u-columns. 3. G_slow⁻¹ by preconditioning: R ≈ mid⁻¹, ‖I − R G_slow‖ ≤ 4.97e-4, and the Neumann form X = I + E X. 4. H, then ρ₆ₐ. | B | w centre | ρ₆ₐ (review) | ρ₆ₐ (original) | |---|---|---|---| | I103-macm3 | x̂ (as run) | [0.079007505696, 0.079007505696] | 0.2309898799 | | I103-macm3 | p̂ (the final step only) | 0.079007505561 | | | I104-win2 | x̂ (as run) | 0.079006909111 | 0.218 | Why the original's value is three times larger: its `acb_mat.inv` encloses G_slow⁻¹ with radius up to 4.11 on entries no larger than 1.538 (cond 1.5e3). A float evaluation at the midpoints gives 0.07894. This also explains why ρ₆ₐ "moves with every radius" (#110, #111). **The centre.** `lemma6_jump_M.py` takes the box centre from the box file's key `x`, falling back to `FPM.ZEROS[5]`. `certify_M2.py export6a2` writes the centre under `p` and has no `x`. So the M = 5 run used wf = 0.999228404 ± 1e-18 in the start box, the flow and T, while the certificate's p̂₁ = 0.99922840320656778…. The M = 3 run avoided this by adding `x = p^` to its input file by hand (commit c3701d9, `data/A_M_6a_M3_1e-10_in.json`). `b_float.py` integrates the flow and its variational matrix in double precision by a second route: the (P, V, C) u-form of §1 in numpy with DOP853, then the chain rule at both ends. - At w(x̂) it reproduces mid(B) to 9.6e-13, which is 6e-8 of B's radius. So B's midpoint is confirmed, at the w the run used. - At w(p̂) it moves by up to 2.8e-6, which is 0.178 of that entry's radius. So the right B very probably lies inside the stored B, but this is not proven. - Its control (wf + 1e-6) lands 225 radii outside. **Not re-checked:** - The backward Lohner flow. - B₁ (export6a, the certificate's box run). - Lemma S(5) and the flat estimate's L and weights, apart from the final weighted norm. - The implication "ρ₆ₐ < 1 ⇒ ψ ≡ 0". I did not read §4.2, so I did not check that the formula for ρ₆ₐ is the right one. ### Mutations | lemma | mutation | review | original | |---|---|---|---| | 6b₁ | sign: V_u = +V/2 in the defect, row 17 (10 discs) | 0 of 10 certify (low coefficients do not vanish) | 0 of 10 certify | | 6b₁ | sign, row 0 discs 0, 18, 37 | 0 of 3 certify | 0 of 3 certify | | 6b₁ | tile (9, 5) dropped | FAIL: (9, 6) agreement point, (10, 4) not connected, point not covered | FAIL: (9, 6) agreement point, (10, 4) not connected, point not covered | | 6b₁ | row 9's stored r × 1.01 | FAIL: C1 design mismatch | FAIL: "row 9: other design" | | 6b₁ | G₀'s radius × 1.01 (402 → 406.02 > ρ₀ = 405) | FAIL: C6 s₀ not in G₀, C7 (0, 0) agreement point | FAIL: s₀ not in G₀, (0, 0) agreement point | | 6b₁ | disc radius × 1.01 in lemma D (row 17, and row 0 discs 0, 37) | still certifies, Λ about +2% | still certifies | | control | my transcription against `SysUM.rhs` and `.lin` with the sign flipped | mismatch 1.1 (clean: 2e-16) | | | control | `ray_hp`, w × (1 + 1e-12) | rows 1–3 outside by 4e4 to 1e5 radii | | | control | `lohner_float`, w × (1 + 1e-6) | 30 of 33 outside | | | 6a | coords: (1 − iμw) at ξ_a | ρ₆ₐ = 1.715, fails | ρ₆ₐ = 3.412, fails (I103) | | 6a | partial: only J_{D,1} = 0 | G_slow 13 × 17, fails | the same (I103) | | 6a | Bscale: B's S rows × 5 | ρ₆ₐ = 3.392, fails | ρ₆ₐ = 6.761, fails (`--load-B` of the review's file) | | control | `b_float`, wf + 1e-6 | 225 radii outside B | | A disc radius × 1.01 is not a falsifying mutation. At Λ ≤ 0.34 the larger disc is still analytic, so both codes rightly certify it. The radius mutations that must fail are the record's r (a design mismatch) and G₀'s radius (a real gap at s₀), and both codes fail both. The sign mutation is caught in both codes by the defect's low coefficients, not by Δ. The swap mutation of 6a needs the flow, so it was run in the original only (I103: step-size underflow). ### What the code proves, against the statements **6b₁(5)**, over the box X = p̂₃₉ ± h of the stored runs: X is axis-aligned in all six parameters, p̂ is truncated to 39 digits, and h = 1e-18 plus arb's radius rounding of 2.2e-27. Grant three things: the C¹ start data at s₀ encloses y⁺(s₀; x) and its x-derivatives, `validated_int.Lohner` is correct, and y⁺ is analytic on G₀ = {|u| > 402, −3π/4 − 0.4 < arg u < 0}. Then the code proves that y⁺ extends analytically to G₀ ∪ ⋃T_jk ⊇ {25 ≤ |u| ≤ 260, −3π/4 ≤ arg u ≤ 0}. This matches statement 5.1, and the bands in fact chain to 419.4. Assumptions the statement does not make: 1. `lemma6b1_cover.check` does not recompute any disc. It trusts the `ok` flags in the stored rows, and the rows do not store the disc inputs. So the certificate cannot be re-verified from stored data alone; this review had to rerun the Lohner flow. 2. The check's C1 tests h and the row radii, but not `ray.json`'s centre `x` or the rows' M. The centre is asserted only at run time, by `row_run`. 3. G₀'s radius 402 and angle 0.4 are hard-coded (`CONF[5]["g0"]`, `G0_ANG`). The link to lemma S at R₊ = 0.0064 (1/(R₊ sin 0.4) = 401.2) is a comment, not a check. 4. C8 checks the bands cover [25, 260]. At M = 5, G₀ starts at 402, so the cover of 260 < |u| ≤ 402, which Ω needs, follows from conditions asserted for other reasons (b₀ > ρ₀ > g₀ and chained overlaps) and is not itself asserted. The review's check reports it: the bands reach g₀. 5. X contains the Krawczyk sub-box p̂ ± (1e-18, 1e-26, 1e-27) only through arb's radius rounding. The chart is T = [[I₂, 0], [C, I]], so A and ω/ω∞ range over exactly ±1e-18 about p̂₅₀. The truncation p̂₅₀ → p̂₃₉ moves A by 4.6e-39, against a margin of 2.2e-27 from `arb(0, arb("1e-18"))` rounding up. 6. The C¹ sets' planted-truth control (`c1check`) cannot discriminate at h = 1e-18 (I37: the `nov` mutation did not fire). Its discriminating run is at h = 1e-9. 7. `lemma6_common.install()` replaces `validated_int`'s a-priori enclosure: an inflation floor, a step refusal at `MAXREL` = 0.05, and a QR overflow treated as a failed step. These are choices, with containment still tested by `contains`. Not reviewed. 8. The disc-radius negative control (`control`, discs past a branch point must fail) exists only in the M = 1 code. **6a(5).** The statement's third hypothesis is "the backward computation of `lemma6_jump_M.py` … succeeds with ρ₆ₐ < 1", so the statement defers to the code. The code computes ρ₆ₐ < 1 from a B that encloses DΦ for w ∈ W0·(x̂₁ ± 1e-18) with B₁ at the certificate's box. The flat estimate is over x̂ ± 1e-6, which contains p̂ ± 1e-18 since |p̂ − x̂| ≤ 1e-9 by (H1). Assumptions the statement does not make: 1. The box-file centre falls back silently to `FPM.ZEROS` when `x` is absent, which is the gap above. The `inside` check is then vacuous, because it compares `ZEROS` with `ZEROS`. 2. ρ₆ₐ is computed from `acb_mat.inv`'s loose enclosure. The quoted 0.231 is a bound dominated by that overestimation; the tighter bound is 0.0790. 3. `LOHNER_ORDER` comes from the environment (default 24) and is not recorded in the output JSON. 4. R₊ = 0.0064 ≥ √2 Z = 0.006348, a margin of 0.8%, checked in `flat_estimate_M`. 5. B is stored as decimal strings: mid to about 106 digits, rad to 25. Containment on reload relies on arb's mag rounding up.
